problem: The rule (curl fingers from H toward T, thumb gives precession direction) is correct, but the trailing clause "in the sense of the spin" is vague and can be read as saying precession runs the same way as the rotor spin. Precession is perpendicular to H and simply reverses when the spin reverses.
fix: End the sentence at "the thumb gives the precession direction", and add: reversing the spin reverses the precession direction.

where: Section 3, sentence on nutation and precession
problem: "Some syllabi call nutation the wobble and precession the topple" is not a standard usage. In gyrocompass work 'topple' means the rise and fall of the spin axis about the horizontal and 'drift' means the azimuthal motion; neither is a name for precession. The sentence risks teaching wrong vocabulary.
fix: Delete the sentence. If terminology is wanted, write: in gyrocompass texts, 'topple' is the tilt of the spin axis about the horizontal and 'drift' its rotation about the vertical; nutation is the short wobble after a sudden torque.

problem: "Caging locks the rotor" can be read as stopping the rotor. Caging locks the gimbals so the rotor axis is held fixed to the case; the rotor keeps spinning.
fix: Caging locks the gimbals, holding the rotor axis fixed to the case while the rotor keeps spinning. It is used before start and during violent manoeuvres.

problem: Ω = T/H is the steady precession rate only when the torque is perpendicular to the spin axis. The condition is not stated, so a student may apply it to any torque.
fix: Add after the formula: this holds for a steady torque applied at right angles to the spin axis.

problem: "Ω comes out too small by a factor of 2π/60" is easy to read backwards. With ω in rpm the wrong answer is correct answer × (2π/60), i.e. about 9.55 times too small; the phrase names a number below 1 as the factor.
fix: Convert to rad/s first; with ω in rpm the answer is too small by a factor of 60/(2π) ≈ 9.55 (it is multiplied by 2π/60).

problem: The node note gives H = Iω = 50.3 with no unit, while the caption and text use kg·m²/s. Numbers should carry units everywhere.
fix: Change the note to 'H = Iω = 50.3 kg·m²/s'.
